header_summary:
spscand, developed by Zenul Abidin, is a privacy-focused scanner for BIP352 Silent Payments, supporting various block sources including Bitcoin Core, BlindBit Oracle, and BIP158 filters. The tool processes only confirmed blocks, employs advanced privacy measures such as randomized SOCKS5 proxy credentials and Tor support, and exposes a local API and webhooks for integration. Detailed architecture, performance benchmarks, and source code are provided at the [spscand GitHub repository](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand) ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/05fbac98-5a91-4224-ad9b-745441252e26n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#ma8201f1e47129be61257f5a0a3141cb879821f1e)).

Testnet5 is now live, with public libbitcoin nodes at wormer.libbitcoin.net:18353 and carmine.libbitcoin.net:18353, facilitating BIP54 support and public peer connections. Node status, configuration details, and blockchain explorers are available at [Libbitcoin public configuration](https://libbitcoin.org/configuration/public.html) and [wormer explorer](https://wormer.libbitcoin.net:58143) ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/HY8DsUoVVHnLe80I6KVSNBpFNJpn8DI7Uf89FfWuKuKMAMAqJHDP5rmpPZi6zVp3JT2Px08Bncryhu05fxBioQ5_v2COC1r2LjncC6vNpFo=@pm.me/T/#u#m6fd1d1fb2dd1a81b7316378e77efec400601632c)).

A proposed P2P protocol upgrade introduces ML-KEM-768-based key establishment, enhancing post-quantum security for encrypted peer communication. Both the protocol design and its operational flow are detailed in the [FIPS 203 specification](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/Events/2025/workshop-on-guidance-for-kems/documents/papers/kemeleon-paper.pdf) and [BIP-324 mediawiki](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0324.mediawikielligatorswift-encoding-of-curve-x-coordinates), with feedback solicited on parameter choices and bandwidth considerations ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/12a1a76d-0e27-4035-9fe8-a47524729c47n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m85f1ad08dcf59870a50431a82801279a866e9c93)).

Recent updates in Lightning Network security address an exploitable closed-channel bug where attackers could trigger denial-of-service using error messages and channel_id collisions. The smite testing tool is being improved to detect such vulnerabilities, with ongoing efforts documented in [this pull request](https://github.com/lnfuzz/smite/pull/257) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/disclosure-dos-vulnerability-fixed-in-core-lightning-v26-06-8/3072/3)).

Advances in Bitcoin protocol validation suggest that maintaining commitments to per-block undo data and focusing on UTXO set updates offers long-term robustness and adaptability, especially for protocols like swiftsync. Validation strategies emphasizing UTXO set commitments are detailed in [this discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-stark-proof-of-bitcoins-utxo-set-at-block-972-500-with-circuits-proven-in-lean/3070/3), highlighting efficiency and resilience to protocol changes.

recent_posts.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
recent_posts.summary: - spscand detects and tracks silent payments with strict privacy by supporting multiple block sources and proxies.  - libspscan securely executes core logic, enables efficient integration, and exclusively relies on public keys for outputs.  - Performance and privacy are validated through extensive tests, supporting correct operation and secure user anonymity.

recent_posts.title: Testnet5 Launch
recent_posts.summary: - Two public libbitcoin nodes on testnet5 are accessible at wormer and carmine addresses.  - Users can monitor these nodes' status and configuration at libbitcoin.org's public node status page.  - Web explorers for blockchain inspection are available at wormer and carmine explorer URLs.

recent_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
recent_posts.summary: - A proposal introduces ML-KEM-based key establishment to protect P2P traffic against future quantum threats.  - Payloads include encapsulation keys and ciphertexts as per FIPS 203, enhancing connection security.  - Feedback is requested on the ML-KEM parameter set choice and advertising encapsulation keys by default.

recent_posts.title: Silent Payments for Electrum
recent_posts.summary:
- A new open source scanner, spscand, enhances Silent Payments and integrates with an existing plugin.
- It monitors sp1 addresses, supports privacy through local data sources, and features Tor integration.
- Users receive comprehensive tools for managing Silent Payments, with ongoing improvements encouraged through feedback.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerability fixed in Core Lightning v26.06.8
recent_posts.summary:
- A specific bug enabled attackers to crash the system by sending error messages at no cost.
- Testing tools initially failed to detect this vulnerability due to a lack of error message support.
- Comprehensive fixes now validate channel identifiers, addressing related vulnerabilities across most implementations.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Header validation relies on proof of work, median time, and block version checks without zero-knowledge proofs.  - Commitments to per-block undo data and UTXO set updates strengthen block validation and network security.  - Focusing on UTXO set verification allows more efficient, adaptable validation compared to traditional per-block mechanisms.

active_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
active_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format, bc1z, introduces quantum resistance using the ML-DSA-65 signature scheme.  - The format enhances security and privacy, revealing the public key only upon transaction spending.  - Community feedback is sought regarding design, deployment, migration, security, and the urgency of proactive adoption.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal aims to improve stale rate observability and block propagation diagnostics in Bitcoin.  - Nodes supporting `staletip` share information about stale tips using BIP 434 `feature` messages and strict policies.  - Technical measures limit shared data to recent tips and maintain network efficiency and security.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Transport Feature Negotiation
active_posts.summary: - A new protocol enables negotiation of transport features like encryption and authentication in Bitcoin communication.  - Nodes exchange specialized packets listing supported features, using header bytes and payloads for identification.  - The protocol streamlines handshakes, maintains backward compatibility, and supports future feature expansions.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal identifies critical vulnerabilities in Bitcoin's protocol and suggests targeted security improvements.  - Solutions include adjusting mining difficulty, restricting legacy scripts, and protecting merkle root computation.  - Some proposed changes spark debate, especially block size reduction and technical standardization, due to scalability concerns.

active_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
active_posts.summary: - The project analyzed Lightning network gossip, revealing faster message propagation and notable network inefficiencies.  - Channel_update and node_announcement messages showed high volumes, suggesting rate limit concerns and implementation issues.  - Future plans include expanding infrastructure, inviting community contributions, and offering raw data for independent analysis.

active_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts.summary: - The integration of k-of-n multisig with Lightning Network increases security and flexibility for users.  - Implementing these multisig setups faces protocol, privacy, and security challenges requiring protocol modifications.  - Proposed BOLT protocol changes seek to improve multisig compatibility and support seamless Lightning Network transitions.

today_in_history_posts.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Proposed changes enhance SegWit sighash by committing to absolute fees and scriptPubKey, improving security.  - The three new sighash flags and OP_MASK opcode offer selective commitment and script component mutability.  - The approach seeks to balance adaptability, explicitness, and robust security without introducing unnecessary flexibility.

today_in_history_posts.title: Approximate assignment of option names: please fix!
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Rusty Russell distinguishes between local and global bit feature masks in his post.  - He suggests promoting local bits to global if they need to be advertised, citing "wumbo."  - Rusty requests users to edit their bits accordingly so he can assign bit numbers soon.

today_in_history_posts.title: CTV, APO, CAT activity on signet
today_in_history_posts.summary: - BIPs 118, 119, and 347 have introduced new, flexible transaction scripting capabilities to Bitcoin.  - APO, CTV, and CAT opcodes have enabled advanced transaction structures, security features, and experimental applications.  - Transaction monitoring reveals CAT's high adoption, innovative contract structures, and active developer experimentation continue.
